speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Foreign Affairs what considerations are used to determine if and to what extent consular support is provided to Singaporeans abroad who are arrested or charged with offences when the Ministry is informed of the incident by the individual concerned, by his or her next-of-kin or by other Government agencies.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: We constantly remind Singaporeans who are visiting, working or living overseas that they have to abide by the local laws.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: Above all else, the entire process has to be in accordance with the local laws and regulations.

speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
text: But, again, and I need to emphasise this, all this is subject to the approval of the local authorities.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Just to confirm, so, if there is a request made to MFA from the next-of-kin or from a person who is incarcerated, and if it is permitted, if it does not contravene local laws, can we assume that MFA would generally extend some kind of consular assistance to every such request?
